behavior: `RadioGroup` never exposes the input of a disabled radio in `inputElement`. It exposes the checked input when that input is enabled, or else the first enabled input in the document, or else `null`. An input in a disabled `<fieldset>` is disabled too, unless it is in the first `<legend>` of that fieldset, as HTML says. After a radio, the group or a fieldset becomes disabled, `inputElement` is thus the same as when they are disabled at the mount. A form library that focuses `inputElement` for an error then focuses an enabled radio. Base UI keeps the input in `inputRef` when its radio or its group becomes disabled, and skips it when they are disabled at the mount. Base UI reads the `disabled` property of the input, which a fieldset does not change, so its `inputRef` also gives an input in a disabled `<fieldset>`. The browser does not focus a disabled input, so with Base UI such a library moves no focus.
